newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Philips Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Philips Q3 results.

text.p: Philips posted Q3 net of 123 million guilders against 539 million in year-earlier period and warned of one billion guilder Q4 charge.
Following is a selection of analysts' comments:
Joost van Beek, analyst at Van Meer James Capel -
"Very disappointing. When you look at the breakdown it is particularly disappointing in the lighting and semi-conductor areas. I was already quite pessimisitc but this surpasses that.
"What I'm looking for now is for them to come up with a good strategic view. So, I still have a wait-and see attitude."
On the Q4 charge:
"The (Q4) charge is huge and disappointing," said Frits de Vries of Gilissen.
"The outlook for the rest of the year is not all that good," he said, adding that software and services, components and lighting had shown disappointing third quarter results.

"Looking at the breakdown of the third quarter I see just one positive point," he said, noting that consumer products showed a big profit increase in the third quarter after posting a year-earlier loss.
"Looking at the figures for Software & Services, this makes me think that PolyGram, as part of this sector, will show a much lower third quarter result," De Vries added.
PolyGram announced a profit warning on Wednesday
Corne Zandbergen, analyst at Generale Bank -
"Disappointment all over the place. Almost every sector is disappointing except perhaps consumer electronics. In lighting it is disappointing to see margins under such pressure.
"In components, the bad result could have been expected."
"Regionally, Asia is not growing as fast as it was, and that is worrying."
"The billion guider charge can be taken positively. (President Cor) Boonstra has again shown that he really intends to improve the whole company."
Jean-Paul van Bavel of Van Lanschot Bankiers:

"I'm most astonished about the breakdown of the group's profit," he said, adding that sectors which had been doing well earlier, such as Lighting and Software & Services, were showing a decrease. "That is very disappointing.
Van Bavel said the planned restructuring charge was much bigger than expected.
He said the big questions for 1997 were whether Consumer Electronics could continue to build on a surprising third quarter recovery, and whether Semi-Conductors would improve earnings.
